english.title: Resist / wilfully obstruct a stopping officer.
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) resisted or wilfully obstructed **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) who was exercising the powers as a stopping officer
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66C(2) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
resisted / wilfully obstructed exercise of powers as a stopping officer

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence was inserted into the Road Traffic Act 1988 by regulation 2 of the Road Vehicles (Powers to Stop) Regulations 2011. S.I. 2011 / 996 refers.
english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant resisted or wilfully obstructed a stopping officer appointed by the Secretary of State under section 66B of the Road Traffic Act 1988, in the exercise of

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

powers as a stopping officer.

other.penalty:
One month imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
